title: iOS: on_focus_in() starts the CoreAudio driver even when the dummy driver is active, causing two concurrent audio mix threads and EXC_BAD_ACCESS crashes
body:
### Tested versions

- Observed in production crash telemetry from a shipped iOS game across export templates from 4.6-era and 4.7-era builds (13 months of App Store crash data).
- The code path is present in 4.6.3-stable and is unchanged in current `master` (checked 2026-07-01): `OS_AppleEmbedded::on_focus_in()` still calls `audio_driver.start()` unconditionally.

### System information

iOS 18 / iOS 26 devices (iPhone 13 through iPhone 17 generations observed), Metal (mobile renderer), official export templates

### Issue description

On iOS, if `AudioDriverCoreAudio::init()` fails at launch, Godot falls back to the dummy audio driver — but the next app foregrounding starts the half-initialized CoreAudio unit anyway. The result is **two threads concurrently running `AudioServer::_mix_step()`**, which is not thread-safe against itself (mutual exclusion relies on each driver's own lock). The two mixers race per-playback resampler state and end-of-stream removal, producing use-after-free `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` crashes inside `AudioStreamPlaybackResampled::mix` / `AudioStreamPlaybackWAV::_mix_internal` / `AudioStreamPlaybackOggVorbis` decode at effectively random addresses/offsets.

The chain:

1. `OS_AppleEmbedded` owns `AudioDriverCoreAudio audio_driver` as a member and registers it with `AudioDriverManager` (`drivers/apple_embedded/os_apple_embedded.mm`).
2. `AudioDriverCoreAudio::init()` can fail at launch for environmental reasons (app launched during a phone call, backgrounded/prewarmed launch, audio session unavailable). Note the render callback is registered *before* `AudioUnitInitialize` is called, and the `audio_unit` is **not disposed** on any failure path (`drivers/coreaudio/audio_driver_coreaudio.mm`, `init()`).
3. `AudioDriverManager::initialize()` then silently falls back to `AudioDriverDummy`, which becomes the singleton and spawns its own mix thread (`AudioDriverDummy::thread_func`) that runs the real `_mix_step()` loop. These sessions have no sound.
4. On the next `applicationDidBecomeActive`, `OS_AppleEmbedded::on_focus_in()` calls `audio_driver.start();` **directly on the CoreAudio member, without checking whether it is the active driver singleton** (`os_apple_embedded.mm`, line ~781 in 4.6.3). `AudioDriverCoreAudio::start()` only checks `!active && audio_unit != nullptr`, so the leftover unit is started and its render callback begins invoking `AudioServer::_driver_process()`.
5. From then on, both the dummy thread and the CoreAudio render thread mix concurrently until the process crashes.

Production evidence — a single crash log (Godot 4.6-era template, app v1.0.12) captured both threads mid-mix at the same instant:

```
Thread 21 Crashed:
0   AudioStreamPlaybackResampled::mix(AudioFrame*, float, int) + 240
1   AudioServer::_mix_step() + 1164
2   AudioServer::_driver_process(int, int*) + 272
3   AudioDriverCoreAudio::output_callback(...) + 264
4   libEmbeddedSystemAUs.dylib  ausdk::AUInputElement::PullInput(...)
    ... (AURemoteIO render thread)

Thread 15:
0   oggpack_look + 100
1   decode_packed_entry_number + 40
2   vorbis_book_decodevv_add + 108
...
5   AudioStreamPlaybackOggVorbis::_mix_frames_vorbis(AudioFrame*, int) + 80
6   AudioStreamPlaybackOggVorbis::_mix_internal(AudioFrame*, int) + 452
7   AudioStreamPlaybackResampled::mix(AudioFrame*, float, int) + 356
8   AudioServer::_mix_step() + 1164
9   AudioServer::_driver_process(int, int*) + 272
10  AudioDriverDummy::thread_func(void*) + 160
```

Exceptions are `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS)`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS`/`KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE`, at varying addresses, typically crashing at `AudioStreamPlaybackResampled::mix + 240` (the `internal_buffer[idx]` cubic-interpolation reads) — consistent with the playback object being freed/recycled underneath one of the two racing mixers.

Every symbolicated crash log in this cluster (13 of 13, spanning a year of releases of one game, 200+ affected devices) shows both mixer threads alive, and crashes occur on both threads (some logs crash on the dummy thread instead). Xcode Organizer scatters these across many differently-named buckets (`NO_CRASH_STACK`, `caulk::semaphore::timed_wait`, `_dispatch_sema4_timedwait`, various `_mix_internal + N` offsets), which hides the combined volume — for the affected title this is by far its largest crash source.

Suggested fixes (either or both):

- Guard the focus handlers: only touch `audio_driver` if it is the active driver, e.g. `if (AudioDriver::get_singleton() == &audio_driver) { audio_driver.start(); }` in `on_focus_in()` (and same for `stop()` in `on_focus_out()`).
- Make `AudioDriverCoreAudio::init()` clean up on failure (`AudioComponentInstanceDispose(audio_unit); audio_unit = nullptr;` on the error paths), so a stray later `start()` is a no-op. This also avoids leaking the unit.

A secondary papercut worth noting: when this fallback happens the player gets a permanently silent game with no recovery path — a retry of CoreAudio init on foregrounding would be a nice follow-up, but the crash fix is the important part.

### Steps to reproduce

The trigger is environmental (CoreAudio init must fail at launch), so it can't be reproduced deterministically from a project alone:

1. Cause `AudioDriverCoreAudio::init()` to fail at launch on a device — e.g. launch the app during an active phone call, or (deterministically, for testing) patch `init()` to `return FAILED;` after the render callback registration.
2. Observe the fallback warning ("All audio drivers failed, falling back to the dummy driver") and that the dummy driver is active (`AudioServer.get_driver_name() == "Dummy"`); the game is silent.
3. Background and re-foreground the app (`on_focus_in`).
4. The CoreAudio unit starts; audio output resumes while the dummy mix thread is still running. Any project actively playing several streams (short one-shot SFX churn accelerates it) crashes within minutes with the stacks above.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A — any project that plays audio exhibits it once the driver-init failure occurs; the defect is in the platform layer (`on_focus_in`), not project content. Happy to provide full sanitized production crash logs on request.
